summary: Thomas Best Jervis was an indologist and historian who held positions with the East India Company (~1813–1841), the Survey of India (~1819–1841), and the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Thomas Blom Hansen, a scholar of indology and history, studied at Aalborg University (MSc 2013–2018). He held posts at Edinburgh, Yale, Amsterdam, the University of Natal, and became Professor of Anthropology at Stanford University in 2010.

Thomas Bond Lindsay worked in indology and linguistics, studying at Wesleyan University and Boston University (Ph.D. ~1882). He taught at Newton High School (1877–1888) and served as Assistant Professor of Latin and Sanskrit at Boston University (1878–1909).

Thomas Borchert, a Buddhist and religious studies scholar, completed doctoral studies at the University of Chicago under faculty including Bruce Lincoln and Donald K. Swearer. He served as Associate Professor of Religion at the University of Vermont (attested 2017).

Thomas Bruce Ridgeway worked in computational linguistics and indology. He earned his PhD from the University of Washington by 1986, where he also served as Director of the Center for Computing and Humanities from ~1986 to 1994.

Thomas Burrow was an indologist and linguist who studied at Christ's College, Cambridge (PhD) under E. J. Rapson. He served at the British Museum, SOAS, and was Boden Professor of Sanskrit at Oxford from 1944 to 1976.

Thomas Callan Hodson worked in linguistics and indology, studying at The Queen's College, Oxford. He served as Registrar at Queen Mary University of London, Principal of Thornsey Training College, and Reader of Ethnography at Cambridge (1926–1937).

Thomas Candy, who studied at Magdalen College School, was an indologist and linguist. He served at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute as Superintendent in 1837 and as Principal from 1851 to 1857.

Thomas Chalmers was a religious studies scholar who studied at the University of St Andrews and the University of Edinburgh. He later held posts at the University of St Andrews (~1823–1828) and the University of Edinburgh (~1828–1843).

Thomas Christian Tychsen was a scholar of linguistics and history who studied at Kiel and Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne. He served at the University of Göttingen as Professor of Theology (1785) and Professor of Philosophy (1788).

Thomas Cleary was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. He studied under E. Bruce Brooks, earned a Ph.D. from Harvard University, and obtained a JD from the University of California, Berkeley.
Thomas Craven worked in linguistics and indology. He completed an M.A. at Northwestern University and earned a B.D. at Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary.

Thomas Doctor works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Ka-Nying Shedrub Ling and conducted doctoral research at the University of Lausanne under Tom Tillemans, later holding a post at the Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Thomas E. Crow is an art historian who studied at Pomona College and UCLA. He taught at multiple universities, served as director of the Getty Research Institute (2000–2007), and became Rosalie Solow Professor at NYU in 2007.

Thomas Edward Colebrooke was an indologist and historian who studied at Eton, East India Company College, and under Jagannatha. He served as President (1864–1882) and Vice-President (until 1890) of the Royal Asiatic Society.

Thomas Erskine Perry, an indologist and historian, studied at Trinity College, Cambridge (BA ~1828) and the University of Munich. He served as a judge on the Supreme Court of Judicature at Bombay (1841–1852) and on the Council of India.
Thomas Ethelbert Page was a scholar in linguistics and history. He studied at Shrewsbury School and St John's College (~1869–1873), and later held a post at Charterhouse School from 1899 to 1936.

Thomas Freeman Yarnall works in Buddhist studies, indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Washington and Columbia University (PhD 2003 under Robert A. F. Thurman), where he became Executive Editor (attested 2007).

Thomas Fulton Cummings, a linguist and indologist, studied at Westminster College and Union and Pittsburgh theological seminaries. He taught at Jhelum Theological Seminary, Biblical Seminary in New York, Union Theological Seminary, and Drew University (1918–1933).

Thomas George Percival Spear was an indologist and historian who studied at St Catharine's College, Cambridge. He held posts at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (1924–1940), Selwyn College (1948–1963), and the University of Cambridge (1963–1969).
